title: Better Posture Linked to Better Decision Making and Mood
gist: A new study in the British Journal of Psychology reports that poor posture affects decision making, and is designed to fix a confound in prior expansive-posture research: earlier experiments prompted participants into postures, so effects could have come from the prompt rather than the body position. The teaser sets up the design without reporting results.

insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: If replicable, workspace ergonomics becomes a cognitive-performance lever, not just an injury-prevention one.
